page: UpCloud GPU-96xCPU-960GB-4xB200 is a KVM-hypervised server configured with an x86_64 CPU architecture. The system features 96 vCPUs with a shared CPU allocation model and 960.0 GB of system memory, yielding 10.0 GB of RAM per core. It integrates four NVIDIA Blackwell B200 GPUs, providing a total of 768 GB of VRAM.

This server configuration does not include local storage, requiring external storage solutions for persistent data. It includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. A key architectural tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation, which may introduce resource contention compared to dedicated CPU configurations, though the massive GPU and memory resources offset this for accelerator-heavy workloads.

Given the presence of four NVIDIA B200 GPUs and 960.0 GB of system memory, this server is designed for large-scale GPU-accelerated workloads. The hardware profile is optimized for deep learning, large language model training, and complex data science jobs. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high density of Blackwell-generation GPU accelerators and system memory provides a specialized platform for workloads where GPU compute and VRAM capacity are the primary bottlenecks.
